failure_summary: Render-layer defects dominate: runs 2/3/4 leak raw cNrM cell notation into coach prose (OI-194) because the zone handles are the only pointer offered for c2r5/c2r4 and the reading key teaches cNrM, and the assembled prompt self-contradicts by rendering openingContext.centrality.text ('Column 4 sits in more of those lines than column 5') directly above a guardrail forbidding any centrality/difficulty comparison (centralityComparison.qualitative is null while betterHasMoreLines is true); run 1 is a separate model-side collapse (production-fidelity run on gpt-5.4-mini, so prompt_confusion cannot be separated from model capability) that production would have RETRIED under OI-183 since it omits the required you-key-line handle and never names column 4.
notes: Sub-sampling per rubric: A3/A4/G2/G4/G5 graded on runs 0-1 only; nulls elsewhere are 'not scored', not passes. A5b N/A (player===1). All named cells verified against the engine's own lostResource.finalMovestring 33322232332414001244445556666660011 and opponentPunishment.finalMovestring 3332224310123223040056500555444456666611 via visualize_board.sh: c2r5 is a real gravity-top major threat for you completing c2r5-c3r5-c4r5-c5r5 (all X) on the 35-ply projected board, and c2r4 is the opponent's real winning disc completing the c4r2/c3r3/c2r4/c1r5 diagonal (all O) on the 40-ply board -- G4/G5 pass, no vector_error. A5 fail runs 2/3/4: raw 'c2r5'/'c2r4'/'c2r5-c3r5-c4r5-c5r5' printed to the player (OI-194, known open); run 3 also echoes the field name as 'that opening resource' (lostResource). G2 fail runs 0/1: guardrail bans a difficulty comparison the vector does not supply, yet run 0 says 'Column 4 was the tougher opening choice' and run 1 says 'their central reply gives them the tougher continuation' -- the latter is also backwards, the opponent's reply is a forced win, not a tougher continuation. A4/G1/A7b fail run 1: it instructs 'keep the 7-shaped double threat alive by playing the [zone:future:c2r5]square...' -- c2r5 is not playable now (column 2 is empty, the next disc lands at c2r1) and is 28 plies out, contradicting the render's own Decision block (better move = column 4); 'their central reply' promises a specific reply that is never named. G7 fail run 1 (judgment half only; mechanical G7a/G7b membership passed): the you-future-fork handle is bound to a phrase used as the move to play, a semantically wrong binding, and the required you-key-line handle is omitted entirely. A6 copied verbatim from grade_mechanical.mjs. annotationRepairs empty on all 5 runs. A7c not charged: the mechanism rests on a fork whose creating square (c2r4 on your own line, ply 35) is never named, but no *-fork-pivot handle exists in render_decision.zones.aliases, so the pivot was never offered.
